theme: Airbnb corporate open source (airbnb org) and public data pipelines built on Airbnb-internal-style data; Airbnb Data Science blog notebooks; Airbnb Newsroom scrapers

candidates.name: airbnb/knowledge-repo
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-sourced platform (Python/Flask, ~5.5k stars, last push Sep 2024, Apache-2.0) that Airbnb's own data science team built internally to publish and search knowledge posts/notebooks. It is the PUBLISHING TOOL itself, not a repository of Airbnb's actual data-science blog content — no ABNB business notebooks, KPI figures, or datasets are committed here. Would only matter if someone stood up a public instance seeded with real Airbnb DS posts, which does not appear to exist.
candidates.why_useful: Directly matches the 'Airbnb Data Science blog notebooks' theme hint but is a dead end for data: it explains why Airbnb's real internal DS notebooks are not on GitHub (they lived inside a knowledge-repo instance, not this repo).

candidates.name: airbnb/chronon
candidates.what_it_holds: Airbnb's open-sourced feature-serving/ML data platform (actively maintained, pushed as recently as 11 Sep 2026). Infra code only (Scala/Python for feature pipelines, online/offline joins) — no Airbnb business data, KPI history, or datasets shipped. Confirms Airbnb's ML infra is public but its data is not.
candidates.why_useful: Closest thing to 'public pipelines built on Airbnb-internal-style data' in the org, but it is a generic ML feature-store framework other companies also use; no ABNB-specific figures inside.
candidates.size_hint: active infra repo, no data files

candidates.name: airbnb/aerosolve
candidates.what_it_holds: Airbnb's older (2015-era) open-sourced ML library, originally built for internal pricing/personalization models (per Airbnb eng blog history). Code and toy example data only, no real listing/pricing data; largely dormant now.
candidates.why_useful: Historical artifact of Airbnb's internal pricing-ML tooling; confirms no real price/demand data was ever released alongside it.

candidates.name: airbnb/airpal
candidates.what_it_holds: Web UI for PrestoDB that Airbnb built for internal analysts to query its Hive/Presto warehouse. Pure query-tool code, no data, effectively unmaintained (description only, last real feature work years ago).
candidates.why_useful: Shows what Airbnb analysts used to query internal data; no data itself. Marginal.

candidates.name: airbnb/reair
candidates.what_it_holds: Hive table/partition replication tooling open-sourced by Airbnb data infra team. No data, infra utility only.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Airbnb's data-infra open source is pipeline plumbing, not data.

candidates.name: oxylabs/how-to-scrape-airbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Vendor (Oxylabs) tutorial repo with Python code to scrape live Airbnb search-results and listing pages (price, availability) at scale via their proxy service. No committed dataset, just scraper code + docs. 7 stars, updated Jun 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Could theoretically extend the fee-panel search-page capture the team already runs (gap #2, realised/asking price), but it scrapes airbnb.com directly beyond the sanctioned capture and needs a paid proxy backend — a ToS decision, catalogue-only per repo rules, do not run.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps the fee-panel search-page capture already running

candidates.name: omkarcloud/airbnb-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Scraper that pulls live Airbnb listings, nightly prices, availability, host profiles, amenities and reviews to JSON across 67 country sites. Commercial 'playground' product with a free-tier code sample; no data committed to the repo itself. 5 stars, updated Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Same category as above — a method for asking-price/availability capture, not a held dataset; scraping airbnb.com directly is out of the sanctioned scope per repo rules.
candidates.size_hint: script + hosted API, no data files
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps the fee-panel search-page capture already running

candidates.name: data-scrape/airbnb-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Small MIT-licensed script to scrape Airbnb listings, prices, reviews and host data. No committed dataset, minimal activity (1 star).
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — another airbnb.com direct scraper, out-of-scope to run per repo rules; catalogued for completeness only.

queries_run: gh search repos "airbnb newsroom scraper" --sort stars
gh search repos "airbnb data science" notebook --sort stars
gh search repos --owner airbnb --sort stars (full org listing, ~50 repos)
gh search repos "airbnb open source data" --sort stars
gh search repos "airbnb press release" scraper --sort updated
gh search repos "airbnb press room" OR "airbnb newsroom" --sort updated
gh search repos "airbnb api client" python --sort stars
notes: This theme is largely a dead end for actual ABNB business data. The airbnb GitHub org (~50 public repos, checked in full via `gh search repos --owner airbnb`) is entirely engineering/design tooling open-sourced for recruiting/brand purposes (JS/CSS/Ruby/Swift style guides, Lottie animation renderers, Epoxy/Mavericks Android libs, visx charting, knowledge-repo, chronon, aerosolve, airpal, reair, streamalert, synapse/nerve service discovery) — none contain committed KPI data, pricing data, or business datasets; Airbnb has never open-sourced booking/listing/financial data itself. 'Airbnb newsroom scraper' and 'Airbnb data science notebook' searches returned either UI clone projects (static HTML/CSS practice clones of the newsroom page with no real press content) or nothing relevant. Generic 'airbnb-data' topic and 'airbnb open source data' searches surfaced only the excluded category: single-file Kaggle-NYC-2019-style EDA notebooks with no new data, which per instructions are out of scope. The only marginally relevant finds are three third-party scrapers of live airbnb.com pages (oxylabs, omkarcloud, data-scrape) — these are 'method' repos per the CONTEXT.md rules (catalogue, do not run; scraping airbnb.com beyond the sanctioned fee-panel capture is a ToS decision for a human). Two WebSearch queries were blocked mid-run because this session had already exhausted its 200-query web-search budget (from other subagents sharing the session budget), so this scout relied entirely on `gh search`/`gh api` (used 6 of 6 allowed `gh search repos` calls plus 2 `gh api` metadata checks, both well within their own limits) plus the two pre-exhaustion attempts. Recommend a follow-up scout retry the WebSearch angle ("airbnb engineering blog dataset", "airbnb newsroom RSS archive") once the session-wide search budget resets, since that channel never actually returned results here. No numbered CONTEXT.md gap is filled by this theme; closest miss is gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy) via the airbnb.com scraper repos, but they only capture live asking prices, not realised/booked prices, and are explicitly out of the sanctioned scraping scope.
